body: Good example on why some features should not be bundled into the core but go as a separate package.
Seems that every new `directive`/`pipe` would be a regression then.

Generic problem, we can not override directives at all. Imagine you are happily using forms module, but want to override `required` validator - you can not... One way is to create your own `my-required` or something. Angular could change selectors to use `:not([NgDisableRequired])`, but it is not elegant either.

Yep, additional attributes for turning off behaviour looks not friendly and will escalate the mess quickly.

As the current solution i propose to remove exports for `min/max` directives ASAP and any mentions in the docs. While not too late. But hold their code and then export them within new solution for directives scoping. (I understand it is a bit radical)

My further proposal is to separate things that are not essential out of core, OR at least out of Forms Module. 
And scope each directive under named module, like `ValidatorRequiredModule` (alternatively under npm package `@angular/contrib` with `ValidatorRequiredModule`).

Since only NgModule is true scope for the directives. This will unlock to "override" logic of directives that match names of standard html attributes and generally be more flexible with directives that are shipped with angular itself.

The downside of this would be frustration from existing users (I used to import only FormsModule, now i need to import 3 modules in order to use standard browser functionality!!! RAGE RAGE  RAGE  etc!)

Related issues that suffer from limitation of overriding directives: 

- https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/17296 - email validator - something that developers expect regardless of conforming to html5 spec

- https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/17485 - feat. request for adding delay timeout `routerLink` - doesn't look like good addition to the core, but would be cool to use different directive under the same name

For now, we are going to remove the exports for the min/max validator directives, as their addition is a breaking change. At the least, we should wait to add them until a major version. In the meantime, we will have further discussion about what the best solution is going forward for all validator directives.

issue.body:
With 4.2, we introduced the min and max validator directives. This was actually a breaking change because their selectors could include custom value accessors using the min/max properties for their own purposes.

For now, we are rolling back the change by removing the exports. At the least, we should wait to add them until a major version. In the meantime, we will have further discussion about what the best solution is going forward for all validator directives.

Closes #17491.

cc: @hansl @IgorMinar

issue.title: min Attribute on Input Type Number Not Working
issue.body:
## I'm submitting a ... 

[ ] Regression (behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[x] Bug report 
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
## Current behavior Using Angular 4.2.4, the `min` attribute on an HTML `input` element with `type="number" is not working with Angular. The browser sees it correctly and stops the arrows from allowing you to go below the minimum, but Angular still considers it valid when you manually type a number below the min. ## Expected behavior Angular should consider the element invalid if the `min` rule is violated. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions https://plnkr.co/edit/TGxvz8STg6WAIPWnShpe?p=info In the above plunker, the button should become disabled when any number below 1 is entered. As it is set up now, it does not work. If you change `min="1"` to be `pattern="[1-9]\d*"`, the intended behaviour occurs. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? Support for `min` was added to [the form validators](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/forms/src/validators.ts) in 4.2.0. ## Please tell us about your environment 

Angular version: 4.2.4


Browser:

- [x] Firefox version 53

For Tooling issues:

Others:
I tried this in Chrome and Firefox with my app and Firefox worked, but not Chrome; however, when I tried the Plunker I made, neither worked.
